about.title: Roseville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Roseville sits where I-80 meets a fast-growing grid of suburban arterials, and the collision records reflect that mix. In 2025, Placer County's largest city logged 808 injury collisions, with 1,156 people hurt and 7 lives lost. Public records show the heaviest counts along I-80, Pleasant Grove Boulevard, Douglas Boulevard, and Cirby Way, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when commuters and shoppers share the same lanes. If you were one of the people injured, the days after a crash can feel scattered: medical appointments, a car in the shop, calls from an adjuster you did not ask to hear from. LawProactive exists to take one piece off your plate. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Roseville residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency. You pay nothing to be connected, and the attorney charges no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Roseville Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines that vary more than people expect
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident injury claim, but if a public agency or its vehicle was involved, the window can shrink to six months. An attorney can sort out which clock applies to your crash before it runs.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you shared some blame; your award is simply reduced by your percentage. That matters in merging and lane-change collisions common on I-80, where insurers often argue both drivers contributed.

items.title: Protection before you talk to the other insurer
items.desc: The attorneys in our network work on contingency and can step in early, helping you preserve photos, dashcam footage, and repair records while declining the other carrier's request for a recorded statement on your behalf.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use casual remarks about how you feel or what you saw to shrink your claim later. Report the crash to your own carrier as your policy requires, but keep it factual and brief.

items.question: My crash was on Pleasant Grove Boulevard and I think I was partly at fault. Do I still have a case?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than eliminated. If a jury found you 20 percent at fault, for example, you could still recover the remaining 80 percent of your damages. An attorney can review the police report and scene evidence to evaluate how fault is likely to be assigned.

items.question: How much does it cost to be connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we do not charge you for the connection. The independent attorneys in our network take car accident cases on contingency, so there is no attorney fee unless money is recovered for you. You can ask the attorney about their specific percentage before you decide to hire them.
